output.reason: A few days of right-hand numbness and tingling worse at night, with reported absence of weakness, facial droop or speech change, fits a common nerve-compression pattern manageable with self-care guidance and a clear escalation trigger.
output.patientMessage: You can start with self-care now: avoid sleeping with the wrist bent, try a neutral wrist splint at night, and take breaks from repetitive hand use. Night-time tingling in one hand often comes from nerve compression at the wrist. Call 911 if sudden weakness, face droop or slurred speech appear. Message us if hand weakness, dropping objects, or constant numbness develops, or if symptoms persist beyond a couple of weeks.
differential: Median nerve compression at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome)
Other peripheral nerve compression or irritation, e.g. thoracic outlet or cervical radiculopathy

redFlags.concern: Trauma, swelling or severe pain in the arm

output.vitalSigns: No vital signs reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
